steps.text: Stir together the brown sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, olive oil, rice vinegar, lime juice, garlic, ginger, and Sriracha in the crock of a slow cooker. Add the ribs; cover and refrigerate. Allow ribs to marinate in the refrigerator for 8 hours or overnight.
Before cooking, drain marinade and discard. Cook on Low for 9 hours. Drain cooked meat and shred, using 2 forks.

raw_recipe.headline: Asian Style Country Ribs
raw_recipe.description: this is a super slow cooker recipe for country ribs that is tasty, versatile, and EASY! Serve with sushi rice and your favorite stir-fry vegetables.
raw_recipe.name: Asian Style Country Ribs

recipeInstructions.text: Stir together the brown sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, olive oil, rice vinegar, lime juice, garlic, ginger, and Sriracha in the crock of a slow cooker. Add the ribs; cover and refrigerate. Allow ribs to marinate in the refrigerator for 8 hours or overnight.
Before cooking, drain marinade and discard. Cook on Low for 9 hours. Drain cooked meat and shred, using 2 forks.

review.reviewBody: I followed the recipe with the exception of the slow cooker. Instead, I baked in the oven at 350 degrees WITH the remaining marinade for about an hour or until tender. DELICIOUS - the marinade flavor stayed in the meat and was really good. Spoon the drippings over the meat. Will make again.

My husband (Filipino) walked into the house after work and started singing John Denver's Take Me Home Country Road...the aroma is beyond awesome and the taste was positively delicious. Yes, I did make changes. First of all, I increased the brown sugar to about 1/2 cup. Sesame oil is potent and to not overpower the taste of the sauce, I waited until I had all the other ingredients added and then carefully, measured out the sesame oil. It amounted to 1/8 cup and was perfect. You could definitely tell the oil was there but it did not overpower. I did not marinate the meat. I made the sauce in my slow cooker and then put the ribs in on top and cooked them on high for 8 hours. The meat fell off the bones. There was enough leftover for hubby's lunch the following day. Three people in his office asked for the recipe after he heated it up in the microwave!! Awesome recipe, saved and looking forward to many repeats!!!

I love the versatility of this recipe. Having almost forgotten about some ribs I had in my fridge, I was searching for a tasty/quick/easy way to prepare them. Since I didn't have time in one day to marinate them and then cook in the slow cooker, I followed another reviewer and decided to marinate them, for about 7 hours, then roast them. I substituted apple cider vinegar for the rice wine vinegar, garlic powder for fresh, and Braggs liquid aminos for the soy sauce. I reserved about 1/3 the marinade to heat up and use as sauce later. After marinating, I drained most of the marinade off because a lot of liquid collects in the pan, spread some large chunks of onion and red peppers over the top, covered them with foil and roasted at about 375F for 45 minutes. Took off the foil and cooked about 10 more minutes to bring up to 145F internal temp. They were done perfectly. Served with jasmine rice and green salad with Asian flavors vinaigrette. Will definitely try this in slow cooker for comparison. Tip: lining roasting pan with foil makes clean up so much easier as these leave a greasy/sticky mess .. as most yummy things do ;)
Thanks Aliskill!

I rated this recipe a few days ago and as I was writing, it occurred to me that this could make the most amazing moo shu pork. So tonight I made it again, just as written (but again using only 1/2 the soy sauce called for in the recipe). I did choose to cook the ribs in the marinade in the slow cooker. Once cooked, I then removed the ribs from the slow cooker and put them (in their marinade) in the fridge until dinner time.
 Hours later, I removed the fully cooked ribs from the refrigerator, drained them of the marinade, and put them on a very hot propane grill (charcoal may be even better) where I allowed them to sear and get some char on the edges--just 4 or 5 minutes flipping them halfway through. I let them rest 5 minutes to ensure that the heat distributed throughout the rib meat. 
 To plate, I simply broke a rib into chunks and placed it on a leaf of butter lettuce with a tablespoon of prepared basmati rice. Holy smokes. That's the best moo shu I have EVER had. Even better if you add a bit of crunchy, vinegar-based cabbage slaw on top.

Delicious!! Only addition I made was adding a bit of honey and a little extra ginger. Wasn't spicy at all, so the kids loved it. If I make it again for adults on,y I'll add some more siracha. As others suggested I baked in oven at 350 for about 1 hour 15 mins. Yummmmm. Will make again.

We love this. We are making more Asian recipes and I am liking some "heat" in my food. Do not like slow cookers so did this in a 350 oven. Kept the marinade to baste if needed. One tip on the salt concerns. I use coconut aminos instead of soy sauce since even lower salt soy sauce is too salty . Will make again for sure.

Stayed pretty close to the original recipe. Marinated overnight in the crock (ribs were mostly submerged and coated the rest of the way around), and cooked all day the following day (unintentionally going a few hours overtime) without discarding any marinade. This extra time may have dried it out a little bit but it was so tender it wouldn't so much fall apart as simply explode the moment touched by a fork/utensil. Reheating subsequent days didn't toughen it up too much, so long as the moisture was kept in. I accidentally (multitasking) used several times too much spice and it wasn't a problem, came out flavorful but not at all painful. Soy aminos (I use Braggs but probably any will do) in lieu of traditional soy sauce can help with the saltiness. I thickened up the leftover juices/marinade combination using flour to make a gravy (unhealthy but delicious) which was good both for serving reheated ribs (keeps in moisture) and for flavoring rice as a side dish - it makes a LOT, still finding ways to use that up, but I don't like waste and I do like the flavor. A good recipe made great by its resilience to human error, trivial prep, and negligible cleanup.

These turned out really good, though I did make some changes. I used tamari instead of soy and cut it in half. I marinated overnight, then baked the ribs in the marinade, covered, at 325 for about 1 hour 15 min. I poured off the marinade into a skillet and reduced it a bit, then poured off the fat. I turned up the oven to 450 and let the ribs brown for a few minutes. I served with stir fry veggies and rice, spooning some sauce over everything. Made a delicious rice bowl!

Yes and yes. I'll definitely make this again. I switched from slowcooker to Instant Pot pressure cooker so after marinating the ribs all day, I dropped them into the pressure cooker an hour before dinner and they cooked in just 40 minutes! Served them along with rice and Bangin' Brussels Sprouts (3 min in the Instant Pot). Not a drop left over after 4 adults finished. I'll double the batch next time.

Good flavor, but just a wee bit salty from the soy sauce, and we even cut it back to half the amount. Only used half the sesame oil and that was plenty for flavor, I thing it would be overpowering otherwise. Used tabasco sauce for the Sriracha. We baked it, covered, at 325 for about 1 1/2 hours and did not shred. Tender and juicy.

After carefully reading all reviews, I tried this. As I was making the marinade, I could already tell things were wrong (taste tested as I added items). The marinade did not taste like lime or ginger so I ended up increasing it to 6 T lime juice and 5 T (minced "prepared" found in produce section) ginger. There was also not much vinegar flavor so I added 6 T rice vinegar (I really love a vinegar taste to shredded pork so I needed to taste it). I reduced the soy to 2/3 c to avoid it being too salty. And in the end I increased the brown sugar to 1/2 c due to the vinegar and lime being a bit sour. I left out the garlic, as our family doesn't care for it. So then I put in the meat and stuck it in the fridge to marinade. 4 hours into the marinading I realized I didn't plan dinner that night, so I decided I would go ahead and cook the ribs for dinner that night. After 1 more hour marinading, I stuck it on 6 hours on HIGH in my crock, marinade left in (bc I was sure they would dry out w/o it--very good decision BTW). After about 5.5 hours I checked them and they were done--almost dry but with the marinade they were great. Taste was FANTASTIC...only thing I would change is decreasing the sesame oil...not sure how much bc it was only SLIGHTLY overpowering...some said switching the olive and sesame but that's not the solution bc then you lose the sesame essence which is one of the biggest reasons it called ASIAN ribs...maybe just use a little over 1/8 c sesame? I will make this again!

I followed the advice of cooking them (pork loin country ribs) in the oven, covered at 350, like some of the other reviews suggested. They were delicious and tender. I did not have sriracha and didn’t miss it.

My family has been making a very similar recipe for as long as I can remember. It was one of my favorite meals growing up and my kids love it as well. . “Country ribs” isn’t specific enough though. If you’re making this in a crockpot, make sure you get pork shoulder country ribs, not pork loin country ribs. Pork loin will be too dry after a long slow cooking.
fantastic I didn't have the Sriracha sauce.... still excellent

Normally the first time I make a recipe I make it as written. After reading several reviews stating that the meat dried out I was having second thoughts in making this recipe. I re-read Rosie's review and decided to take her advice and give it a try. I followed the recipe directions as written but instead of using our slow cooker I used a covered baking dish. I baked it in the oven at 350 degrees with the marinade for 1 hour. I was very pleased at the results. The meat was tender and juicy with a lot of flavor. I will definitely make this again. Thanks for the advice Rosie!
The only thing I did differently was cooked in oven, with rice and chop suey veggies
Super easy ingredients to mix and marinating is a must. I used a pressure cooker for 12 minutes. Phenomenally delicious!
delicious! The substituted red pepper flakes since I didn’t have hot sauce
Have made this multiple times since it was first published yrs ago. Absolutely love it, altho have to make it sparingly with my husband's low sodium diet...

Although this smelled wonderful while it was cooking, I thought this was just ok. Despite cooking it less time in my slow cooker, the ribs were still dry. I wound up using the marinade and making a pork stir fry with brown rice. I probably won't make it again.
